items.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal Calls for WTO-Compliant Approach to Correcting Global Trade Distortions at the Concluding Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, U.S.
items.summary: Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Shri Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people, and is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in global supply chains.

facts.text: Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Shri Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people, and is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in glob…
He said Most-Favoured-Nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system, ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest trader and the largest trader.

Shri Goyal said measures at the border must be based on specific and verifiable evidence rather than presumptions about entire countries, regions or sectors, and must respect due process and WTO rules.

India supports the objective of eliminating forced labour and voluntary exchange of good practices among G20 members, provided that such cooperation does not involve monitoring of members, create new obligations or result in information being used as a basis for unilateral trade action.

bullets: Est. 1 Jan 1995; HQ Geneva ; 166 members (TH, Apr 2026); DG Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (TH, Mar 2026); India a founding member of both GATT and WTO .
WTO is the third pillar of the world economy, with the IMF and World Bank.

MFN: no discrimination among trading partners; national treatment: imports treated like domestic goods once inside . US unilateral tariffs (2025-26) violate MFN and bound-rate obligations (TH, 26 Mar 2026).
India: 18th in merchandise exports, 1.8% share (WTO Global Trade Outlook, April 2025; IYB 2026).

bullets: Established 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, after the Uruguay Round; replaced the GATT (1947/48) system, with GATT surviving as an integral WTO agreement.
HQ Geneva ; one-country-one-vote, consensus-based decisions.
Membership: 166 (TH, Mar 2026) (older notes say 164); latest members Comoros and Timor-Leste (2024) .
WTO widened governance beyond goods to services (GATS) and intellectual property (TRIPS) and added a rules-based dispute mechanism.

bullets: ~12% of India's land is prone to floods and river erosion (NIDM Annual Report 2023-24; PYQ 2025).
Worst-hit: Brahmaputra valley ("sorrow of Assam"), Kosi and Ganga plains (Bihar, UP), coastal deltas (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Odisha, WB) hit by Andaman Sea depressions (UPSC CSAT passage).
Himalayan rivers swell in monsoon and flood frequently; cloudburst flash floods are rising in the Himalaya and NE (IYB; LENS Jul 2025).
Mitigation: embankments, drainage channels, sea dykes, real-time flood forecasting (e.g., 37,760 sq km flood-prone area protected in West Bengal - IYB state chapter).

Also along the Vamsadhara and Pennar and in Nellore, Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and Guntur.
AP's most fertile soils, ~6% (CDI; APP gives ~5%). They are porous and loamy, rich in potash and lime, and hold moisture well; each flood renews them with silt (CDI; APP).

bullets: National Monsoon Mission launched 2012 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (IITM Pune + IMD) .
IMD is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). The National Monsoon Mission began in 2012: phase 1 2012-17, phase 2 2017-25 (IYB 2026).

Mission Mausam was launched 14 Jan 2025 with IMD Vision 2047, at Rs 2,000 crore. IMD, NCMRWF and IITM implement it (IYB; LENS Apr 2025). It built the Bharat Forecast System (6 km resolution, 10-day rain forecasts). India has 47 Doppler radars (14 in 2014).
In May 2026 IMD unveiled a block-level monsoon forecast model. It blends AI with nearly a century of data from the Kerala onset date (TH, 13-14 May 2026).
Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT): average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean down to the 26 deg C isotherm. It is measured in Jan-Mar and predicts monsoon rain better than SST .

items.title: Robotics to Become an Accelerating Tool in Every Specialty of Medicine: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
items.summary: He said robotics, together with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and nanoscience, would create a larger ecosystem for precision health delivery and precision medicine, with emerging technologies enabling increasingly personalised healthcare based on an individual’s genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns.

facts.text: Dr. Jitendra Singh was delivering inaugural address at the International Conference of the "Society of Robotic Surgery" here.

It will happen everywhere,” he said, adding that while the present conference is focused on robotic surgery, the future could see the emergence of robotic medicine, robotic endocrinology and robotic cardiology, just as AI is finding applications across different medical specialties.
He said undertaking such detailed genetic sequencing for a population of 1.4 billion would require the optimal use of AI and robotics.
Dr. Jitendra Singh congratulated the organisers of SRS India 2026 for bringing robotic surgery into the domain of institutional learning, academics and professional conference platforms.

sections.topic: Ambedkar's social thought · Conversion to Buddhism
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 1 History & Culture › A-6 › Ambedkar's social thought - annihilation of caste, state socialism, conversion to Buddhism › Conversion to Buddhism - year, date, place, vows, followers, name
bullets: Yeola declaration: at the Depressed Classes Conference, Yeola, 13 October 1935, he announced he would leave Hinduism ("born a Hindu... will not die a Hindu" ).
Considered Sikhism (supported by B.S. Moonje; opposed by Gandhi, Rajagopalachari, Malaviya); dropped it fearing "second-rate status" among Sikhs.

Died 6 December 1956, Delhi, weeks after the conversion. (CDX dates the conversion to 1935 - that was only the Yeola declaration.)

bullets: Rises at Chemayungdung glacier (Kailash range), east of Mansarovar; 2,900 km long, only 885 km in India; 9th largest river in the world by volume.
Dibang and Lohit join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya; the combined river is the Brahmaputra (IYB).

Right bank (north, Himalayan): Subansiri, Kameng (Jia Bhareli), Manas, Puthimari, Pagladiya, Sankosh; Teesta joins in Bangladesh. Left bank (south): Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri (Nagaland hills), Dikhu [GK for bank convention] (UPSC notes label Subansiri/Manas "left" - the standard convention treats the north bank as right).
Teesta: 414 km; rises at Tso Lhamo lake (North Sikkim); largest tributary Rangeet; draft 2011 sharing treaty still stalled (LENS Jul 2026).
